# Whole-space operator obligations for the hierarchy

The user authorized the complete 0.2.1 plan with corpus completion as the goal.
The first desired sized-Xor source is retained in the authoring sessions. Before
accepting sizes, close the whole-space unitarity obligation of the supported
hierarchical denotations, then extend the actual bound rules and finite leaves.
No `.qli` size syntax, external schema or production receipt is enabled by this
proof packet alone.

Use the existing `HierarchicalOperators` complex coefficient definitions as the
subject. Prove both inverse laws on the complete finite basis for identity,
wire permutations/structural adapters and ideal dyadic phase; prove closure under
sequence, tensor, inverse, coherent control and literal powers. Include zero
width/count and keep phase in the controlled branch. Connect these laws to
actual structural typing and constructed definition/meaning denotations; a
unitary annotation or equation between two arbitrary maps is insufficient.

This separate Mathlib interpretation may use mathematical matrices, but the
executable checker must never materialize them above six-bit leaves or expand
shared repeats. Reuse all existing public declarations and auditors. Keep source
and compilation failures if a first proof attempt needs repair. Required native
counterexamples continue to include phase, axis, count and malformed zero-body
mutations. Preserve the explicit finite Rust-leaf/native/transport boundaries;
those become later proof obligations rather than assumptions hidden in a seal.

The recursive checkpoint now discharges child unitarity through successful
actual evaluation and extracts every typing premise from `Derivation.checkAll`.
`HierarchicalAcceptance.checkAll_unitary` constructs the common physical/logical
entry denotation and its `UnitaryInterface`; its inverse/reference corollaries
cover any successful entry denotation. The evaluator still rejects finite,
call, computed and observation/initialization bodies. Extending those semantics
requires compatible successor interfaces and the same evidence obligations;
this checkpoint does not silently broaden the existing evaluator or checker.
